polymorphic-collections.label: Polymorphic Collections
polymorphic-collections.summary: Use one shared method call across mixed objects so callers do not need type-specific branches.

sketch-0.title: Different objects can answer the same call
sketch-0.bodyMarkdown:
Polymorphism lets one caller use the same behavior across different object types.

```python
alerts = [
    EmailAlert("Server restarted"),
    SmsAlert("Build finished"),
]

for alert in alerts:
    print(alert.send())
```

The useful part is not merely that the list is mixed. The caller uses one `send()` contract for every object and does not ask which concrete class it received.

Different objects, one method contract, one caller.

sketch-1.title: A service can depend on behavior instead of concrete classes
sketch-1.bodyMarkdown:
A reusable service can depend on shared behavior instead of concrete classes.

```python
def deliver_messages(alerts):
    messages = []

    for alert in alerts:
        messages.append(alert.send())

    return messages
```

The service does not need `isinstance()` branches for EmailAlert and SmsAlert. Any future object that provides the same `send()` behavior can participate.

That keeps the service focused on what objects **can do**, not what exact class they are.
